body.statement:
For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), put
\[
 M_A=(2^{\ell}-1)^4(3^{k+1}+3)^4,
 \qquad
 M_B=M_A\,k(k-1)(2k-1)^4,
 \qquad
 M_{k,\ell}=M_A+M_B. \tag{24}
\]
The design-A and design-B structural enumerations used by \(\mathscr A\) have at most \(M_A\) and \(M_B\) templates, respectively. Every template has a semialgebraic Boolean description with at most
\[
 N_0=4\ell+10k+12,
 \qquad
 S_0=100(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1),
 \qquad
 D_0=4 \tag{25}
\]
variables, polynomial sign atoms, and polynomial degree.

Let
\[
 (A_S,D_S)=\mathsf{Samp}(N_0,S_0,D_0),
 \qquad
 (A_E,D_E)=\mathsf{Exist}(N_0,S_0+1,D_0) \tag{26}
\]
be coordinatewise nondecreasing published record-count and relative algebraic-degree bounds for bounded algebraic sampling and for existential realizability with a sample over the current coefficient field. Define
\[
 R_{k,\ell}=2+M_{k,\ell}(A_S+A_E),
 \qquad
 D_{k,\ell}=D_SD_E. \tag{27}
\]
Then \(R_{k,\ell}\) bounds the total number of algebraic sample and decision records generated by the one-sample/all-chart compiler, and hence its number of retained labeled outputs, while \(D_{k,\ell}\) bounds every final real-univariate algebraic degree after normalization back to \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). If
\[
 Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1,
\]
there is a universal constant \(C\geq1\), independent of \(k\), \(\ell\), and the input, such that
\[
 R_{k,\ell}\leq 2^{CQ^C},
 \qquad
 D_{k,\ell}\leq 2^{CQ^C}. \tag{28}
\]

Over an arbitrary real input field \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), the computation terminates relative to effective field arithmetic, order, sign-determination, and real-root oracles. Let \(\mathsf{Samp}_h\) and \(\mathsf{Exist}_h\) denote the corresponding published integer-height bounds, and let \(\mathsf{Flat}_h\) denote the explicit determinant, square-free-factorization, and root-isolation height bound for normalizing a finite real-algebraic tower to one real-univariate representation. For rational input coordinates whose numerators and denominators have binary length at most \(L\), set
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1),
 \qquad
 h_S=\mathsf{Samp}_h(N_0,S_0,D_0,h_0), \tag{29}
\]
and let
\[
h_E=\mathsf{Exist}_h(N_0,S_0+1,D_0;h_0,h_S,D_S),
 \qquad
 h_F=\mathsf{Flat}_h(D_SD_E,h_S+h_E+1), \tag{30}
\]
where \(\mathsf{Exist}_h\) is evaluated after coefficients are represented in the degree-at-most-\(D_S\) real algebraic extension furnished by the initial sample. Define
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)=\max\{h_S,h_E,h_F\}.
\]
After flattening the extension tower and clearing only guarded denominators, every algebraic target or witness coordinate can be represented by a square-free integer polynomial of degree at most \(D_{k,\ell}\) and rational isolating data of binary length at most \(H_{k,\ell}(L)\). After enlarging the same universal constant if necessary,
\[
 H_{k,\ell}(L)
 \leq
 \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}. \tag{31}
\]
Thus the record/output count and algebraic degree have the singly exponential fixed-alphabet bound (28), while the rational-height guarantee is the separate bound (31). A rational-input Turing implementation terminates. The decision enumerates structural charts, samples one point from their nonempty union, and applies an existential unequal-target test to each chart; connected-component description and target projection are not required decision stages, and no generic two-copy classifier is used.
body.justification: The theorem bounds the actual sampling and existential stages and derives normalized degree by multiplying the initial and relative extension degrees.
body.gap: The prior theorem bounded component, projection, and label stages that the maximal compiler no longer uses and conflated record/degree and rational-height complexity descriptions.
body.consumer: Exact implementations receive singly exponential fixed-alphabet record and degree bounds and a separate, correctly composed rational-height guarantee.
body.proof_tex:
We verify the structural count, the sequential algebraic-degree multiplication, and the rational-height recurrence in the order used by the compiler.

A proxy endpoint \(b_i\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) has a nonempty support, so it has at most \(2^{\ell}-1\) labeled support patterns. The four shared response vertices contribute at most
\[
 (2^{\ell}-1)^4. \tag{32}
\]
At a rank-two cell, there are two endpoint orientations. For each of the \(k\) values of \(z\), positivity of \(v_e(z)\) and the equality \(a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)\) leave three support states: left zero, right zero, or both positive. Thus rank two contributes at most \(2\cdot3^k\) local templates. By \(\mathrm{lem:rank\text{-}one\text{-}lred\text{-}normal\text{-}forms}\), mode \(\mathrm E\) has \(3^k\) coordinatewise split faces, and modes \(\mathrm L,\mathrm R,\mathrm D\) add three more. Allowing either positive-table rank gives at most
\[
 2\cdot3^k+3^k+3=3^{k+1}+3 \tag{33}
\]
local templates per cell. There are four cells, so multiplying (32) by the fourth power of (33) gives \(M_A\).

For design B, every one of the four response links is either a zero-residual link or an active link. An active link records one of \(k-1\) first nonbaseline pivots and one of two pivot signs, giving
\[
 1+2(k-1)=2k-1 \tag{34}
\]
states. A relevance certificate chooses an unordered pair of distinct instrument values and the sign of its nonzero cross-product, giving
\[
 2\binom{k}{2}=k(k-1) \tag{35}
\]
possibilities. The residual-forest exhaustiveness in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) permits multiplication of these independent coarse labels. This yields \(M_B=M_Ak(k-1)(2k-1)^4\), and addition across the two design outputs yields (24).

For (25), retain four endpoint vectors, requiring \(4\ell\) coordinates, and two incident coefficient vectors in each of four cells, requiring \(8k\). In design B, projective common-instrument and optional joint-treatment auxiliaries require at most \(2k\) more coordinates. Population margins, response masses, component scales, and four residual-transfer scalars require at most twelve further coordinates. Hence the number of variables is at most \(N_0\).

There are \(4k\ell\) table-factorization equations. Endpoint simplex and support conditions use at most \(4\ell+4\) atoms; coefficient simplex, support, and split conditions use at most \(24k+8\); residual definitions and transfer equations use at most \(16k+8\); and retaining every proportionality minor uses at most \(4(k-1)^2\). Shared-instrument equations, normalizations, endpoint incidences, cycle consistency, and signed relevance use fewer than \(20(k\ell+k^2+\ell+1)\) additional atoms. Since \(k\geq2\) and \(\ell\geq3\), their sum is at most \(S_0\).

The table equations are bilinear. A residual \(a_{ei}(z)-\rho_z a_{ei}(z_0)\) has degree at most two. Introducing one transfer scalar makes negative proportionality degree at most three, and the four-link cycle product has degree four. Shared-instrument equations have degree two, relevance has degree at most three after substituting the bilinear definition of \(q^X\), and the remaining atoms have no larger degree. Thus \(D_0=4\). The target in (13) is linear, so adjoining the unequal-target condition adds one atom of degree two and leaves the degree bound \(D_0\) unchanged. This proves (25)--(26).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\) to each structural chart over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). The emptiness-and-sampling phase produces at most \(A_S\) algebraic records per chart. If the union is nonempty, choose the first returned sample \(x_0\) and set \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\). A real-univariate representation of \(x_0\) uses one primitive element \(\alpha\) with
\[
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\alpha):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 \leq D_S. \tag{36}
\]
Because \(t_0\) is obtained from \(x_0\) by the linear sums in (13),
\[
 \mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)
 \subseteq\mathbb K_{\zeta}(\alpha),
 \qquad
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 \leq D_S. \tag{37}
\]

Each of the at most \(M_{k,\ell}\) unequal-target tests is now a one-block existential-realizability problem over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)\), with format \((N_0,S_0+1,D_0)\). It creates at most \(A_E\) records. If it returns a witness with primitive coordinate \(\beta\), then
\[
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\beta):
   \mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)]\leq D_E. \tag{38}
\]
The tower law and (37)--(38) give the explicit degree multiplication
\[
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\beta):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 =
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0,\beta):\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0)]
 [\mathbb K_{\zeta}(t_0):\mathbb K_{\zeta}]
 \leq D_ED_S. \tag{39}
\]
Every output coordinate belongs to the field on the left of (39). Multiplication by such an element is a linear operator on a vector space of dimension at most \(D_ED_S\); its characteristic polynomial annihilates the element. Therefore the minimal polynomial of every output coordinate has degree at most \(D_ED_S\). Passing to its square-free factor and selecting the correct real root by Thom signs or an isolating interval cannot increase that degree. This proves the degree part of (27) by multiplication of extension degrees, not by reapplying a complexity slogan to an already enlarged degree.

There are at most \(M_{k,\ell}\) initial sampling calls and the same number of unequal-target calls. Adding the fixed incompatibility and rigid/nonrigid summary records gives
\[
 2+M_{k,\ell}A_S+M_{k,\ell}A_E=R_{k,\ell}, \tag{40}
\]
which bounds all generated records and therefore all retained outputs.

Put \(Q=k\ell+k^2+\ell+1\). Equations (24)--(25) imply, for universal constants,
\[
 M_{k,\ell}\leq2^{CQ},
 \qquad N_0\leq CQ,
 \qquad S_0\leq CQ,
 \qquad D_0=4. \tag{41}
\]
The singly exponential bounds in \(\mathrm{lem:effective\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}sampling\text{-}existential}\), applied to the two formats in (26), imply
\[
 A_S,D_S,A_E,D_E\leq 2^{CQ^C} \tag{42}
\]
after enlarging \(C\). Substitution of (41)--(42) into (27) and absorption of a fixed product and sum into the exponent prove (28).

For arbitrary real input, selected-cell normalization divides only by \(r_e>0\), and chart normalization divides only by a pivot whose sign is part of the chart. Thus every chart coefficient lies in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\). The chart family is finite by (24), and every sampling, existential, sign, and root operation terminates relative to the stated field oracles by the cited algorithmic lemma. This proves field-relative termination.

Suppose now that the coordinates of \(\zeta\) are rational with numerator and denominator lengths at most \(L\). Reconstructing deleted simplex coordinates uses at most \(Q\) additions. Each coefficient in a degree-at-most-four chart atom is obtained using at most \(8Q\) additions or multiplications of these coordinates and recorded pivots. Clearing a product of at most \(8Q\) denominators adds at most \(8Q(L+1)\) bits, and summing at most \(8Q\) resulting terms adds at most \(\lceil\log_2(8Q)\rceil\leq8Q\) bits. Since \(Q\geq1\), the conservative bound
\[
 h_0=64Q^2(L+1) \tag{43}
\]
therefore dominates every initial integer coefficient length. Multiplication by the square of a recorded nonzero denominator preserves a strict sign, so this clearing step does not change a chart.

The integer-height clause of the cited sampling algorithm gives the first recurrence in (29). The coefficients of the unequal-target atom consist of the original chart coefficients and the coordinates of \(t_0\), whose degree and height are bounded by \(D_S\) and \(h_S\). Applying the cited existential height bound over this represented extension gives \(h_E\) in (30). Flattening the tower can be done by multiplication matrices in the vector space of dimension at most \(D_SD_E\): determinants defining characteristic polynomials use at most \(D_SD_E\) products and sums of represented coefficients. The cited square-free and root-isolation algorithms then give the stated \(h_F\). Consequently normalization does not change the degree bound (39).

For each of the two algorithmic stages, the cited height exponent is bounded by \(2^{CQ^C}\) using (41)--(42). The extension-flattening, square-free, and root-isolation exponent is also at most \(2^{CQ^C}\) because \(D_SD_E\leq2^{CQ^C}\). Successive substitutions multiply only a fixed number of such exponents, so, after enlarging \(C\),
\[
 \max\{h_S,h_E,h_F\}
 \leq (h_0+1)^{2^{CQ^C}}
 \leq \bigl[64Q^2(L+2)\bigr]^{2^{CQ^C}}, \tag{44}
\]
which is (31). This height statement is separate from the singly exponential record and degree bounds. Square-free normalization and rational root isolation supplied by the cited algorithm give the claimed integer polynomial and isolating data. All loops and rational subroutines are bounded, so the Turing implementation terminates. The executed stages are exactly chart enumeration, chart sampling, and one-copy existential refinement; neither component enumeration nor target projection enters the decision.
